purpose: Row shapes only superseded code could have written, replayed through the whole migration chain.

shapes.name: done-before-the-event-timeline
shapes.history: Completing work wrote no completion checkpoint before 0010. Migration 0010 derives work_completed strictly from completion checkpoints, so it reconstructs work_created for this item and deliberately invents no completion. No constraint in the chain ever tied done to a completion event, so this reached Phase 11 as a done item with no episode at all.
statements: INSERT INTO projects (id, name, slug) VALUES (CAST(:project_id AS uuid), 'Legacy timeline project', 'legacy-timeline-project')

INSERT INTO work_items (id, project_id, title, summary, status, initial_checkpoint_id, version) VALUES (CAST(:work_id AS uuid), CAST(:project_id AS uuid), 'Decided before events existed', 'Completed while the timeline did not yet exist', 'done', CAST(:checkpoint_id AS uuid), 3)

INSERT INTO checkpoints (id, work_item_id, kind, prompt, source_client, source_session_id) VALUES (CAST(:checkpoint_id AS uuid), CAST(:work_id AS uuid), 'context', 'Historical prompt text, preserved exactly.', 'legacy-client', 'legacy-session')

expectations.description: the completion survives as done rather than being rewritten or dropped
expectations.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM work_items WHERE id = CAST(:work_id AS uuid) AND status = 'done'

expectations.description: no completion event is invented for it
expectations.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM work_events WHERE work_item_id = CAST(:work_id AS uuid) AND event_type = 'work_completed'

expectations.description: it carries generation 0, the value meaning no completion episode
expectations.sql: SELECT completion_generation FROM work_items WHERE id = CAST(:work_id AS uuid)

expectations.description: its only checkpoint keeps its exact historical prompt
expectations.sql: SELECT prompt FROM checkpoints WHERE id = CAST(:checkpoint_id AS uuid)

expectations.description: 0010 still reconstructs the one fact it can prove
expectations.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM work_events WHERE work_item_id = CAST(:work_id AS uuid) AND event_type = 'work_created' AND origin = 'backfill'

shapes.name: completion-checkpoint-before-the-event-timeline
shapes.history: The control case for the shape above. This completion did leave a completion checkpoint, so 0010 can prove it and does backfill the matching work_completed event. Phase 11 must build a real episode here, which is what keeps the legacy exemption narrow.
statements: INSERT INTO projects (id, name, slug) VALUES (CAST(:project_id AS uuid), 'Provable completion project', 'provable-completion-project')

INSERT INTO work_items (id, project_id, title, summary, status, initial_checkpoint_id, version) VALUES (CAST(:work_id AS uuid), CAST(:project_id AS uuid), 'Completed with a completion checkpoint', 'Its completion is provable from stored evidence', 'done', CAST(:checkpoint_id AS uuid), 2)

INSERT INTO checkpoints (id, work_item_id, kind, prompt, source_client, source_session_id) VALUES (CAST(:checkpoint_id AS uuid), CAST(:work_id AS uuid), 'context', 'The original hand-off prompt.', 'legacy-client', 'legacy-session')

INSERT INTO checkpoints (id, work_item_id, kind, prompt, source_client, source_session_id) VALUES (CAST(:completion_id AS uuid), CAST(:work_id AS uuid), 'completion', 'The completion summary as it was written.', 'legacy-client', 'legacy-session')

expectations.description: 0010 backfills exactly the completion event it can prove
expectations.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM work_events WHERE work_item_id = CAST(:work_id AS uuid) AND event_type = 'work_completed' AND checkpoint_id = CAST(:completion_id AS uuid)

expectations.description: a provable completion gets a real episode, never generation 0
expectations.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM work_items WHERE id = CAST(:work_id AS uuid) AND completion_generation < 0

expectations.description: the completion checkpoint and the work item agree on that generation
expectations.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM work_items AS work JOIN checkpoints AS checkpoint ON checkpoint.work_item_id = work.id AND checkpoint.kind = 'completion' WHERE work.id = CAST(:work_id AS uuid) AND checkpoint.completion_generation = work.completion_generation

shapes.name: open-and-abandoned-before-the-status-rename
shapes.history: Before 0012 the lifecycle spelled unstarted work 'open' and had no 'deferred'. Terminal non-done statuses never carried completion evidence, so Phase 11 must carry them forward untouched at generation 0.
statements: INSERT INTO projects (id, name, slug) VALUES (CAST(:project_id AS uuid), 'Status rename project', 'status-rename-project')

INSERT INTO work_items (id, project_id, title, summary, status, initial_checkpoint_id, version) VALUES (CAST(:open_work_id AS uuid), CAST(:project_id AS uuid), 'Still open when the rename landed', 'Unstarted work spelled the old way', 'open', CAST(:open_checkpoint_id AS uuid), 1)

INSERT INTO checkpoints (id, work_item_id, kind, prompt, source_client, source_session_id) VALUES (CAST(:open_checkpoint_id AS uuid), CAST(:open_work_id AS uuid), 'context', 'An open hand-off from before the rename.', 'legacy-client', 'legacy-session')

INSERT INTO work_items (id, project_id, title, summary, status, initial_checkpoint_id, version) VALUES (CAST(:abandoned_work_id AS uuid), CAST(:project_id AS uuid), 'Abandoned before events existed', 'Terminal without ever being completed', 'wont-do', CAST(:abandoned_checkpoint_id AS uuid), 2)

INSERT INTO checkpoints (id, work_item_id, kind, prompt, source_client, source_session_id) VALUES (CAST(:abandoned_checkpoint_id AS uuid), CAST(:abandoned_work_id AS uuid), 'context', 'An abandoned hand-off from before the rename.', 'legacy-client', 'legacy-session')

expectations.description: 0012 renames open to pending rather than dropping the row
expectations.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM work_items WHERE id = CAST(:open_work_id AS uuid) AND status = 'pending'

expectations.description: an abandoned item keeps its terminal status
expectations.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM work_items WHERE id = CAST(:abandoned_work_id AS uuid) AND status = 'wont-do'
SELECT count(*) FROM work_items WHERE id IN (CAST(:open_work_id AS uuid), CAST(:abandoned_work_id AS uuid)) AND completion_generation = 0
